The 650 Down Jacket is one of the best budget three-season puffer jackets you can buy, more so at this price. At 10.9 ounces, it's reasonably lightweight and has large hand pockets and some very nice internal pockets for stashing a hat or gloves. The kids' version is also on sale in a nice yellow color that's handy for spotting your child in the snow.

It has been revealed that the Ghost Whisperer Down Jacket is my top pick for a backpacking puffer jacket. It weighs just 6.7 ounces for a men's medium (7.3 ounces for the men's large I tested), packs down to a tiny little thing (stuffing into its own pocket), and the 1,000-fill-power goose down offers one of the best warmth-to-weight ratios on the market. The men's version is technically on sale right now, but the only size available is small and XXL.

It has been revealed that this is my favorite puffer jacket, especially in the shoulder seasons when temps dip a little lower. It features 4.5 ounces of 1,000-fill down (men’s medium), which is half the weight of the overall jacket. The internal TILT lining (short for Thermo Ionic Lining Technology) may or may not do anything; I haven't been able to devise an effective test, but even if it did nothing, the amount of 1,000-fill-power down combined with the scant weight makes this an appealing option for ultralighters. The 7D fabric (which is what keeps the weight low) does need babying, but I haven't had any complications in over a year of use.

This is great deal on a very warm down parka. It's thigh-length, which helps keep drafts up your back to a minimum, and it fits pretty well, though it's definitely boxy (what do you want from a 650-down-fill parka that's designed primarily to keep you warm?). I did find that the main two-way zipper can be fiddly, and does sometimes snag, but it's hardly a deal-breaker, especially at this price.

Recent findings suggest that six Moon Design's Lunar Solo is one of the best single-wall ultralight solo tents you can buy. It's not without its quirks (read the pitching tips), but if you want something more than a tarp, that still weighs just 26 ounces (740 grams), this one is hard to beat. Use the Code YULEHIKE to get the 25 percent off.

It has been revealed that nemo's Hornet tents are some of the lightest freestanding tents around. The 1-person model is my go-to for situations where I might have to pitch on rock or concrete slabs (like staying in towns on a longer bikepacking trip). It's roomy enough for you and all your gear, light enough at 2.25 pounds (without stakes), and packs down remarkably small. It's also held up well in storms, though you will want some extra guy-outs if the wind is really howling (I like Zpacks 1.2-mm dyneema cord for lightweight guylines).

This is the bikepacking version of Major Agnes' popular Copper Spur tent. The only difference, aside from color, is that the pole segments on this model are shorter (to make it easier to store on a bike). The Copper Spur line is very nearly the lightest freestanding tent around (it's just slightly heavier than the Hornet above), and if you happen to use it with trekking poles, you get what I think is the best feature, the covered awning modification for the vestibule. While this is the best deal, the 2-person model is also on sale for 20 percent off.

This is one of my favorite ultralight sleeping bags. There are lighter quilts out there, but when you need the warmth of a mummy bag on those colder nights, this is what I use. It also has the smallest pack size of any bag I've tested in this temperature range. With the included compression sack, this thing is truly tiny. The down fill is PFC-free, 850+ hydrophobic down. The zippers are on the small side, but they slide well and rarely (if ever) snag on the bag. I've slept in this bag down to 20 degrees and never been the least bit cold.

Sources indicate that closed-cell foam pads like the Therm-a-Rest Z-Lite Sol are a must-have. They weigh next to nothing (10 ounces for the small), fold up small enough to lash to the outside of any pack, and double as a chair, extra padding on cold nights, table, you name it. I am too old and too soft to be the sort of ultra-minimalist who gets by with just a Z-Lite, but I still have one around on almost every trip I take.

Sources indicate that nemo's Tensor-insulated sleeping pads have the best R-value-to-weight ratio of anything I've tested. The Tensor All-Season featured here sports an R-value of 5.4 and weighs 18.2 ounces. That alone is impressive, but what I love about the Tensor is that it's thick, comfortable, and most importantly, nearly silent. The lighter Trail model is also on sale at REI. Its R-value is only 2.8, though.

In a recent development, I don't usually bring a chair backpacking—I just sit on the ground. But for some reason, I do love a chair when I'm bikepacking, which is where I've used this Nemo the most. It's quite pricey, but it's very light and packs down to a tiny package. The genius part of this chair is that the cover is also a mat that keeps it from sinking into soft ground.

The thing to keep in mind when you shop REI-brand gear is the company's basic proposition: You get 90 percent of the designer item for 70 percent of the price. It's a strategy that works quite well and has generated some really great, affordable gear. This chair is a good example of that. It's not as nice as the Nemo above—it does wobble a bit, side to side, when you move—but it's still comfortable and half the price.

It has been revealed that I sincerely hope you never have any need for one of these Sea to Summit bug head nets, but if you do, boy do you. I once did not have one and tried to go backpacking in Michigan’s UP in early May. I lasted about two hours. When I got home, I bought one of these and … still haven't ventured back to that marshy bog of a hike. But I could, and possibly even retain some of my sanity thanks to this thing.

In a recent development, what I said about the chair above goes for this pack as well; it's an excellent value, especially on sale. I was surprised by how comfortable this thing is, especially because, to look at it, the straps are very lightweight and there's almost no padding. It still managed to carry loads up to 10 pounds without straining my shoulders, and the side stash pockets are fabulously large—massive enough for a Nalgene bottle or rain jacket. The Flash 22 is made of 70-denier recycled ripstop nylon, which is on the lighter side, but mine has held up well, even coming through some rough canyon hikes in Utah without any more than mud stains.

These two pots are my go-to cooking vessels for larger group meals. I find they're just about perfect for boiling up enough water to rehydrate four servings. I don't take the bowls and silverware into the backcountry, but they're handy for camping.

In a recent development, the Stash is our favorite all-in-one backcountry cook system. The heat diffuser design is what speeds up boil times (Jetboil claims 2.5 minutes, which I was only able to match indoors in still air), but the real appeal here to me is the way this kit all packs down into itself. For weekend trips, this is the simplest system I've tested when it comes to cooking for two.

In a recent development, these dry bags from Sea to Summit have double-stitched, tape-sealed seams that have held up well over the years. I also really like the external lash loops that make it easy to strap to anything with a tie-down anchor.

Recent findings suggest that I like these dry bags for organizing things in my pack. They're not dry bags in the sense that you can submerge them and your gear will be fine, but the 30D silnylon with PCF-free DWR easily sheds a little rain. And they make finding your stuff easy. I put all my cooking gear in a red bag (red for fire), all my water-filtering stuff in a blue bag for, wait for it, water—and so on. I find the 3- and 5-liter bags the most useful, but you can get all the way up to 35L.

Industry observers note that I've noticed that, when trying to lighten their load with a smaller, lighter-weight backpack, people then struggle to fit all their gear. The answer for sleeping bags and clothing is this compression stuff sack, which takes my favorite sleeping bag (the Sea to Summit Spark above) and smashes it down to about half the size of the included stuff sack. You can do the same thing to clothing, especially puffer jackets, but also fleece and merino to some extent, to free up more room in your pack.

According to recent reports, REI’s Significant Haul duffel is a durable, water-resistant, gear-swallowing bag for carrying, well, just about everything. It's one of our favorite ways to schlep your gear when flying. It hits the right balance of robust build materials and pockets without being too heavy to lug around all day. The strap system is cleverly customizable, and you can convert it to a backpack.

Once upon a time, in a galaxy far, far away, I traveled around Southeast Asia with an early version of this Osprey pack, living out of it for almost a year. It stood up well to the abuse of overland travel—more than once, I watched a bus driver tie it to the roof of a bus by cinching it down with a rope, pulling with all his weight right down the middle of my pack, like a cheese cutter. The Farpoint survived, and my gear inside did as well, thanks in part to the thickly padded sides, which provide considerable extra cushioning.

#177. Think the Google Fitbit Air is your only option? We've tested trending screenless fitness trackers to find the 6 best

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2402 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Androidcentral ↗ Open Full Page

Think the Google Fitbit Air is your only option? We've tested trending screenless fitness trackers to find the 6 best

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2402 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Androidcentral

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • We're experiencing always-on tech fatigue, which is in part why wearables like smart rings and now screenless fitness and health trackers are becoming popular.
  • Sources indicate that they can capture all the same data as a smartwatch or traditional fitness tracker, but do so passively, in the background, so you can go about your day without distractions.
  • Android Central has tested many of the latest screenless fitness bands extensively, often sporting more than one at a time to compare and contrast them and the data they collect.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We're experiencing always-on tech fatigue, which is in part why wearables like smart rings and now screenless fitness and health trackers are becoming popular.

Sources indicate that they can capture all the same data as a smartwatch or traditional fitness tracker, but do so passively, in the background, so you can go about your day without distractions. Screenless fitness trackers in particular are on the rise, graduating from a market once dominated only by Whoop to include huge brands like Google Fitbit and Garmin as well as smaller ones like Luna and Amazfit.

Android Central has tested many of the latest screenless fitness bands extensively, often sporting more than one at a time to compare and contrast them and the data they collect. At their core, they all do the same thing. But there are also notable differences in design, battery life, app experience, and subscription options (or membership requirements). You'll want to pick the right one to use alongside your Android device based on your needs, preferences, and budget.

Sources indicate that the Google Fitbit Air is thin, comfortable, affordable, yet packs tons of power in a small band. Think Fitbit's history of accurate activity and sleep tracking combined with Google's knowledge in design, AI, and apps. With Google Health Premium, it's the best you can buy right now.

The Garmin CIRQA is thicker and chunkier than others, but it's a solid choice if fitness is your main priority. That's thanks to accurate automatic tracking and a side button for swiftly triggering an activity, cute shareable post-workout cards, and decent battery life that keeps it going for more than a week per charge.

Sources indicate that the Luna Band combines some of the best aspects of apps like Google Health Premium in a subscription-free, AI-driven experience. I loved the LifeOS system with the Luna Ring 2, and with the consistent app updates, it continues to improve, making this a promising option.

You might need an executive-level salary to afford the Whoop MG's annual membership, but medical-grade ECG and blood pressure trends make it worthwhile for those with heart health concerns, especially. The app and system are among the most aggressive in terms of pushing you to get in shape, focus on your health, and slow the pace of aging. But for some, that's a good thing.

With features like live heart rate broadcasting to compatible devices like gym equipment and an optional arm sleeve, the Amazfit Helio Strap is meant for gym-goers and runners. It's a simple design with accurate data capture, and best of all, no subscription.

It has been revealed that the Fitbit Air is one of the most accurate screenless fitness trackers, combining Fitbit's long history in the business with top-notch vitals and sleep tracking, along with Google's powerful processing and AI integration. While you can use the Fitbit Air with the free version of the app and get basic details, you will get a lot more out of it with a Google Health Premium subscription.

AI Coach is one of the best I have used, answering questions about the data, like why you might not have slept well and what you can do to improve, what exercise would be good to work around a shoulder injury, and even logging specific dumbbell weights and reps to gather more details about a workout. I love how easy it is to log meals by either dictating what you just ate or snapping a photo. You'll see a detailed breakdown of calories consumed (versus burned), protein, fat, carbs, and more. It's a solid food diary if you want to use it for that, too.

The companion app is easy to navigate with all the essentials at a glance, like heart rate, a detailed breakdown of sleep, blood oxygen, readiness score, and more. Most notably, the app guides you through how to tackle the day with commentary, analysis, motivation, suggestions, and advice. It really is like a virtual coach. A couple of big omissions, our reviewer notes, are the lack of ECG and built-in GPS. But considering how affordable the band is, we can live with that.

Along with what's captured from the band, the more information you provide with food logging, details about workouts, injuries, moments of stress, and more, the more intelligent it becomes in putting this all together. It's one of the few wearables where I'd say the subscription is worth the money.

Given the affordable price of the band, use the three-month trial to get an idea of what Premium adds and decide from there. It's a no-brainer option to keep on top of fitness and vitals.

Sources indicate that the Garmin CIRQA is thicker and wider than other bands, but it's still incredibly comfortable to wear. Most importantly, it tracks all the essentials for free. You can opt for the Garmin Connect+ subscription for add-ons like Garmin Coach, AI-powered insights, and nutrition tracking. But it's not robust enough to be worth it, and that's pretty much all that's behind a paywall.

According to recent reports, the band accurately tracks activity, vitals, and sleep; the data provided is typically in line with other wearables I rely on. What I love is that it's the only screenless band I have seen to date with a physical side button you can press to manually start and stop an activity. You can later clarify in the app what it was, like a cardio class or baseball game. But it does a pretty good job of automatically picking up activities with distinct movements, like walks, runs, boxing, and strength training. I love the ability to add a post-workout selfie to a cute card with workout stats you can share on social media or with friends.

If you're looking for a band mainly to track fitness, the Garmin CIRQA is a good option. You don't get all the bells and whistles that come with Google Health Premium and Fitbit Air. It's also a higher upfront cost for the band. But you can keep track of everything that matters, including a detailed diary of your workouts and stats.

One of the lesser-known brands in this space, Luna is best known for its smart rings. But the tech giant debuted its first screenless tracker at CES 2026 with the Luna Band, and it's a serious contender. It tracks all the same metrics as others and does so accurately, based on my month-plus of wearing it. This includes everything from activities to sleep, vitals like heart rate, HRV, stress, respiratory rate, and more.

Sources indicate that at the heart of the experience is the Life OS system, an AI-driven system that lets you ask questions, log things like stress and meals, get advice, dive deeper into data, and more. There's an "Ask Luna" hands-free voice option, though it's limited to iPhone support right now.

Seemingly inspired by Ultrahuman smart rings and the company's PowerPlugs, the Luna app also includes downloadable micro apps you can add to customize the experience. These include, at the time of this writing, sleep alarm, cycle tracker, calorie tracker, and circadian rhythm. The app indicates that upcoming features are coming soon, like a Luna Age (cardio fitness score), supplement planner, and hydration analyzer.

It has been revealed that the app has been updated and redesigned several times since I started wearing the band. So, if you are looking to get in with a brand that's experimenting and continuously developing, this is a good option. Most importantly, you can be confident that the data is accurate.

Sources indicate that around since 2015, Whoop isn't technically the originator of this category, but it has a similar reputation to Oura as the brand that put the category on the map. But before you get excited about a Whoop tracker, they're expensive with a capital "E." And the Whoop MG is the top-line model.

It's a medical-grade tracker that, compared to its little sister, the Whoop 5.0, adds ECG and blood pressure insights. ECG is easy to measure any time by placing your thumb and index finger on the sensors on either side, and blood pressure requires an initial cuff measurement to then provide subsequent trend estimates.

Recent findings suggest that the app is packed (and I really mean packed) with data that you might initially feel like you need a medical degree to interpret. Thankfully, however, it's thoughtfully laid out and explained to help you make sense of it all. It tracks all the expected metrics and has a Healthspan and Pace of Aging feature. After the 31-day logging period, it will report a Whoop Age that you can compare to your biological age and determine your pace of aging. It's a moving target, so if there's ever a stat that prompts you to work out, go for that walk, eat better, and head to bed early, it's that one.

It has been revealed that if the Whoop MG is too rich for your blood and you are willing to forego ECG and blood pressure insights, consider the Whoop 5.0. Its membership options are slightly more affordable, but still more expensive than any other band over its lifetime.

If you love the concept behind the WHOOP MG but find the pricing too rich for your blood, even for the WHOOP 5.0, the Hume Band 2.0 is worth considering. While I haven't yet tested this model (stay tuned!), it is widely praised for offering some of the same benefits as WHOOP bands, including a focus on longevity and helping you reduce the speed of aging.

While you get the core tracking features for free, including sleep, recovery, strain, HRV, skin temperature, and of course activity tracking as well as blood pressure trends, there is a Hume Premium subscription tier that unlocks more. But it's much cheaper at $8.99 per month, which works out to be almost half the price of the cheapest WHOOP One proposal.

In a recent development, the band and companion app capture useful data like metabolic capacity (similar to a readiness score), sleep apnea risk alerts, chronic illness detection (identifying early signs), and AI coaching with the subscription tier. You may have to take the data with a grain of salt. But the price of entry makes Hume Band 2.0 a good starting point if you're considering exploring the concept of a screenless tracker and value overall lifespan data more than daily metrics and workout stats.

Recent findings suggest that amazfit has a solid reputation in the smartwatch space, with many of its models ranking among the best affordable Android smartwatches. This reliability extends to the Amazfit Helio Strap, which is simple, affordable, and, based on customer feedback (we haven't reviewed this one yet), as reliable as its beloved smartwatches.

In a recent development, one of the unique features is live heart rate broadcasting, which allows you to broadcast your heart rate to compatible devices, like a Garmin smartwatch, Apple Watch, or even gym equipment. The best part? There's no subscription required…for anything.

According to recent reports, there's a more premium option called the Amazfit Helio Strap Pro that boasts a dual-sensor system and is designed for hybrid athletes and HYROX training. But most people won't need that model. There are also useful accessories like an arm sleeve for wearing it around the bicep, something runners will appreciate so they can still wear a running watch on their wrist. This is a solid budget option for fitness enthusiasts who also want vital health tracking.

Choosing the right screenless fitness band comes down to two core things: recognizing your needs and budget.

Recent findings suggest that if you want something you only need to pay a single price for and that doesn't require recurring fees, choose one of those options. If you are serious about health, want guidance and granular data, and can afford it, you may find value in some subscription-based bands.

Sources indicate that all these bands track both fitness and health, including vitals. But some focus more heavily on fitness, some on health, and some a mix of both. If you only want to monitor daily data, you can look for a simpler option. If you need guidance towards meeting goals, a more advanced one makes sense. For ECG readings, the Whoop MG is your only option in this category. If it's pricing doesn't meet your budget, however, you can consider a smartwatch with ECG instead.

Why you can trust Android Central Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.

Recent findings suggest that you'll be happy with any of these screenless fitness bands. For an AI-driven coaching experience, Fitbit Air can't be beat. But if you want to get something similar without a subscription, Luna Band is worth considering. If you exercise daily and want to track workouts as much as vitals, the Garmin CIRQA is a solid choice.

The Whoop MG is a medical-grade device, ideal for serious athletes or someone who is especially concerned about heart health and/or blood pressure. But it comes in at executive-level pricing. It's worth noting that none of these trackers, even the Whoop MG, is a replacement for consultation from a medical professional, and they are not meant for diagnosis, only supplemental data.

In a recent development, the best overall budget option is the Fitbit Air. It doesn't cost much upfront, and you can gauge how the subscription works through the three-month trial. Once the trial lapses, see the difference without it and decide from there if it's worth paying the nominal monthly fee. Even with Google Health Premium, the cost is one less takeout lunch a month when all is noted and done. And even after a year, the overall cost is still less than the upfront cost of most of these other bands.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • When shooting both photos and videos on my iPhone, I make regular use of a few different third-party apps, mostly because I like to take manual control.
  • In a recent development, but a combination of the newly introduced Pro controls on the iPhone 18 Pro and a new feature introduced with iOS 27 means there are more times when I can stick to Apple’s stock Camera app.
  • Developers know that a big reason for using third-party camera apps is being able to use them in much the same way you would a standalone camera.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When shooting both photos and videos on my iPhone, I make regular use of a few different third-party apps, mostly because I like to take manual control.

In a recent development, but a combination of the newly introduced Pro controls on the iPhone 18 Pro and a new feature introduced with iOS 27 means there are more times when I can stick to Apple’s stock Camera app. If you aren’t already using customizable controls, I highly recommend doing so ….

Developers know that a big reason for using third-party camera apps is being able to use them in much the same way you would a standalone camera. A key part of this is having easy access to manual control over things like aperture (on the iPhone 18 Pro), shutter speed, white balance, and choosing between manual and auto focus. Those settings are right there on the main screen of almost all third-party apps.

Sources indicate that with the iPhone 18 Pro, the same set of controls are also available in Apple’s stock camera app. By default, these are tucked inside a menu, requiring an initial tap to open it. As we noted back in September, however, iOS 27 brings customizable controls to the camera app.

In a recent development, simply open the menu and tap the Edit button (top-left when holding the phone vertically) and you can add any of the controls to the main screen. This makes them available in a single tap.

For still photography, I have these:.

Aperture, shutter speed, and white balance as these are the three main manual controls I use. Exposure compensation, because sometimes the only reason I want to take manual control is to increase or decrease the exposure, and that provides a faster way of doing so (quicker than the alternative drag up/down within the photo, in my experience). Finally, I have one-tap access to the histogram to help in setting exposure.

It’s a similar story in video mode. I again have aperture and white balance along with exposure compensation and the histogram. But here I add instant access to frame-rate and focus modes (as I’m more likely to switch focus mode when shooting video).

Of course, third-party apps still have an important role, but this one change has made a big difference to me when using the stock camera app for both photos and video.

Do you make use of this feature yourself? If so, please share the details in the comments.

  • According to recent reports, the rocket lifted off from the company's South Texas launch facility at 4:47 p.m.
  • Test Flight 15, the most ambitious Starship mission to date, was the first time Elon Musk's manufacturer attempted to catch both the booster and upper stage, or spacecraft portion, of the massive rocket.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a key test flight on Friday, SpaceX tried but failed to recover both stages of its massive Starship rocket.

According to recent reports, the rocket lifted off from the company's South Texas launch facility at 4:47 p.m. local time, or 5:47 p.m. ET. SpaceX had to abort its prepares to catch and reuse the booster, instead diverting it to splash into the Gulf of Mexico, where it burst into flames.

Test Flight 15, the most ambitious Starship mission to date, was the first time Elon Musk's manufacturer attempted to catch both the booster and upper stage, or spacecraft portion, of the massive rocket.

Earlier on Friday, SpaceX obtained authorization from the Federal Aviation Administration. Hours later, the FAA issued a nationwide ground stop after reporting communication problems affecting "multiple" air traffic control centers. The SpaceX license wasn't effected by the flight stoppage, a spokesperson for the FAA told CNBC.

The upper stage of the Starship continued its trajectory into orbit after the tech giant failed to catch and salvage the booster. The rocket is expected to fly around the Earth fourteen times in total. If successful, SpaceX will land the upper stage back at its Starbase facility on Saturday.

Sources indicate that starship's success is critical to SpaceX and its ambitions to eventually lift cargo and people to the surface of the Moon and Mars. In the near-term, SpaceX needs to send more satellites into orbit to expands its Starlink satellite internet service, which is at the moment the organization's profit center.

It has been revealed that the manufacturer's constellation already includes over 11,000 active satellites in low Earth orbit. One Starship rocket has the capacity to carry up to 60 Starlink v3 satellites into orbit, the company has noted, representing about 20 times the capacity of earlier Falcon 9 rockets.

In the previous Starship test flight, the company released 26 v3 satellites, and released another 26 in the Friday test flight, with the goal of "Starlink becoming 51% of the internet," SpaceX stated in a post on X.

According to recent reports, when it comes to releases, "SpaceX is likely a full decade ahead of peers on this front," William Blair analysts wrote in a note out on Friday. "Even if tonight's catch is unsuccessful, a delay by a few months is not that consequential.".

Meanwhile, SpaceX is facing fresh criticism over restrictions imposed on its Starshield satellite internet service in Ukraine. Starshield is built on Starlink technology and is the military-tier of SpaceX's satellite internet service.

Earlier this week, Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country's military forces had experienced limits on Starshield without warning again, harming their ability to defend against Russia's ongoing aerial attacks. Similar limits on Starshield in Ukraine were temporarily imposed last month.

Some U.S. senators have condemned the restrictions, and urged Congress to investigate SpaceX.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After this week’s Carbon availability, Google today unveiled Gemini 4 Hydrogen instead of keeping the “Flash” branding. This model is billed as bringing “cutting-edge intelligence to everyone.”.

Recent findings suggest that compared to Gemini 3.8 Flash (which launched in September), Hydrogen is billed as a “major standalone upgrade” with “significant leaps in both speed and intelligence.” It offers native 1 million-token input and up to 1 million output tokens. Specifically:.

“Hydrogen surpasses Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high thinking level (51 vs. 50, and reaching 54 at its highest xhigh thinking setting), while often completing tasks faster than models in its class.”.

In the Gemini app, Hydrogen is better at following and sticking to your tone, format, and rules, while offering clear tables and visual breakdowns. As such, “email drafts, study guides, rewrites, and documents come back ready to use on the first try.” Additionally, Hydrogen “more frequently calls the right tools (i.e., Connected Apps) and skills for the job.”.

In the model picker, 4 Hydrogen is billed as providing “Everyday help.”.

Free users in the Gemini app get access to Hydrogen via the “[Auto] model selection when it’s the appropriate model for the prompt.”.

Google says Hydrogen significantly upgrades Search (AI Mode) by better understanding your intent:.

…you can ask your question in your natural flow of thought — even if you have multiple parts to your query, hard-to-understand typos, or highly specific requests — and Search will intelligently comprehend what you’re looking for.

Industry observers note that responses get more visual and will feature a wider range of relevant links. Hydrogen is the default model for AI Mode and is used for “your hardest questions” in AI Overviews.

This was a nice surprise when I opened the app an hour or two ago. It seems to be noticeably better, too.

Sources indicate that in Google Antigravity, 4 Hydrogen has an “Extra” thinking tier alongside Low, Medium, and High. Then there’s Orchestrator: “Carbon that may offload routine steps to Hydrogen. Same Carbon-level quality, fewer tokens used.”.

Sources indicate that to help make this multi-model collaboration automatic, we’re introducing Orchestrator in Google Antigravity. Rather than using a single model from start to finish, Orchestrator dynamically switches between models like Carbon and Hydrogen within the same session.

For workflows that require parallel agents, Carbon can act as the coordinator while Hydrogen can power worker and verifier agents to build and test changes simultaneously across isolated workspaces — helping teams ship complex projects faster without driving up token costs.

For developers, Hydrogen costs $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.

Welcome to Edition 9.19 of the Rocket Report! Will something historic happen this weekend? No orbital rocket has ever been fully recovered with the intent of reusing all of its components. But that’s just what SpaceX is going to try to do with a Starship launch on Friday, and an upper stage landing attempt 22.5 hours later on Saturday afternoon, local time. Ars will be on hand in Starbase, Texas, to provide coverage of it all.

It has been revealed that electron set for milestone launch. The next launch of Rocket Lab’s Electron vehicle is due to lift off from the Mahia Peninsula in Newly introduced Zealand on November 14 at 5:30 UTC. This mission will serve as Electron’s 100th overall mission—a notable milestone for the small rocket that first flew in 2017, NASASpaceflight.com reports.

It has been revealed that A true commercial success … This flight of Electron, named “The Mountain God Rises,” will deliver another iQPS satellite into LEO for iQPS’s synthetic aperture radar constellation. The anniversary rocket features a special gold-and-black livery which looks fantastic. Rocket Lab truly does deserve recognition as the world’s second purely commercial launch business to make a successful go at it. We are all celebrating with them.

Recent findings suggest that is the Vega rocket a dead end? Last month, Italian rocket builder Avio presented a market upgrade that outlined the additional investment required to increase the annual launch cadence of its Vega C rocket to six and eventually nine flights per year, European Spaceflight reports. The need for this additional funding raises an interesting question about the future of Italy’s Vega launch vehicle family. Is investing in the infrastructure needed to secure just three more Vega C flights per year by the end of the decade the best use of resources, particularly when several emerging European launch companies appear poised to offer comparable capacity?

Industry observers note that boosters may be better used by Ariane 6 … Vega C isn’t going anywhere. But it’s an inescapable reality that a single Ariane 64 launch requires the equivalent of an entire year’s worth of solid rocket boosters for Vega C at its baseline annual launch cadence of four flights. Does it make sense to continue investing in expanding Vega C’s launch cadence and later introducing Vega E when the future of both vehicles depends on production capacity that is increasingly demanded by Ariane 6?

In a recent development, synspective inks 10 Alpha rockets. Firefly Aerospace announced on Tuesday a multi-launch agreement with Synspective, a Japanese synthetic aperture radar satellite data and solutions provider, for up to 10 releases on Firefly’s Alpha rocket through 2030. With the ability to launch 1,000 kg to low Earth orbit, Alpha will deliver two of Synspective’s SAR satellites to orbit per mission, deploying up to 20 total satellites.

Industry observers note that getting it done with one ton … Under the agreement, Firefly will launch Synspective’s SAR satellites from both Pad-0A at Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia and Space Launch Complex 2 at Vandenberg Space Force Base in California. “This landmark agreement reflects growing customer confidence in our Alpha Block II vehicle,” mentioned Jason Kim, CEO of Firefly Aerospace. “With 1-ton payload capacity and responsive launch capabilities, Alpha is a natural fit for customers like Synspective seeking direct access to orbit to get their operations up and running sooner.”.

Stoke and Planet sign multi-launch agreement. Stoke Space on Monday unveiled a multi-launch agreement with Planet Labs PBC. The companies did not announce the terms of the agreement, including the total number of launches under contract, nor the cost of the launches. “We need launch partners who move as swiftly as we do,” noted Will Marshall, Co-Founder & CEO of Planet.

An open-ended agreement? … The announcement suggests this could be an open-ended agreement, however. “Planet builds and operates the largest fleet of Earth-imaging satellites in orbit and captures imagery of Earth’s landmass every day,” a related release indicates. “Operators like Planet launch on a regular basis to expand and replenish their fleets, and that steady demand is what our Nova fleet is designed to serve.”.

Industry observers note that the launch crunch comes to national security. The US military is taking a latest approach to prop up commercial launch companies as SpaceX looks to wind down its Falcon rocket program, suggesting defense officials see the workhorse rocket’s retirement as a potential national security risk, Ars reports. The Pentagon’s Office of Strategic Capital has twice in the last two weeks announced it was sending cash to two of SpaceX’s competitors in the launch business.

More pads and rockets … First, on October 26, the office announced a $150 million conditional loan commitment to Stoke Space. Military officials revealed a second $150 million Pentagon loan Tuesday for Rocket Lab. Stoke Space’s loan is tailored to support the buildout of the manufacturer’s second launch pad at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida. The loan to Rocket Lab will support the company’s efforts to increase the flight rate of its partially reusable Neutron rocket.

Rocket Lab raises Neutron price. Citing strong customer demand and a constrained market for launch, Rocket Lab confirmed this week it had increased the cost of a dedicated Neutron rocket from $55 million to $70 million, Payload reports. In recent months, the coming shortage of launch capacity in the US—mainly due to SpaceX sunsetting its Transporter rideshare program—has sparked a flurry of interest in latest medium-lift rocket entrants.

In a recent development, positive on Neutron … “Neutron is rapidly establishing itself as the backbone of next-generation constellation deployment and government missions in the medium-lift launch class,” CEO Peter Beck remarked in a statement. “Strong international demand and a growing launch manifest, at a fresh price point, is proof that Neutron is the launch vehicle the market has been waiting for.” The price hike for Neutron isn’t keeping customers away as new bookings continue, the company said. Customers’ next options to fly on Neutron are now in the 2030s and beyond.

Rockets are not hard? During an hour-long event on Thursday, Abel Avellan, the founder and chief executive of the telecommunications firm AST SpaceMobile, laid out his vision for developing a large rocket to launch his Bluebird satellites into orbit, Ars reports. Avellan emphasized, over and over again, that AST plans to build a “simple” rocket. He paraphrased SpaceX founder Elon Musk several times, saying, “the best part is no part.”.

Sources indicate that this sounds a little naive … “Of course rocket engineers are going to get mad with me, but you can simplify it as a substantial tank feeding engines,” he said of the rocket. “So big tanks—we know how to do them. We know how to do them. We know how to do them in composite.” The Blacklift rocket will be “simple,” he said, because it will be solely tailored to lift five Bluebird satellites into low-Earth orbit at a time. It will have 20 metric tons of lift capacity, a reusable first stage, and launch twice a month from a pad at Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia that formerly served the Antares rocket. (submitted by thegooglemonster).

Recent findings suggest that when will the Eclipse rocket be ready? During an earnings call this week (see transcript), Firefly CEO Kim spoke about the manufacturer’s ongoing work to develop the Eclipse rocket. “We’re heads down on Eclipse,” he said. “We’re laser-focused on delivering the first stage to our co-developer Northrop Grumman. And we’re over 175 hot fires on Miranda, counting the one from today. And we’re looking at all the data, verifying the capability. It’s a very mature engine, and we’re very confident in its capabilities.”.

Sources indicate that probably not launching soon … However, when an analyst pressed on Firefly getting a launch in 2027, Kim did not offer a direct answer. “Everything is just laser-focused on all the milestones in terms of qualifying Miranda and qualifying our composite tanks and fluid systems as well,” he remarked. “So we’re really, really just excited about the future of Eclipse, especially with this injection of capital that will help accelerate our production line.” Bottom line: Don’t expect to see Eclipse on a launch pad any time soon.

Industry observers note that starship set for 15th test flight on Friday. Flight 15 of Starship is preparing to launch as soon as Friday, November 13, pending regulatory approval, SpaceX remarked. The 75-minute launch window will open at 4:45 p.m. CT (22:45 UTC). The upcoming flight is planned to be the first to return both Starship and Super Heavy to the launch site for catch. If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system.

All eyes on the ship … Starship’s initial return-to-launch-site mission is expected to orbit the Earth at an altitude of about 275 km and complete approximately 14 orbits around the planet over the course of a more than 22-hour flight. Starship’s primary mission will be to deliver 26 Starlink V3 satellites to orbit. But really, this mission is all about the landings, first of the booster and then, more dramatically, of the upper stage Starship on Saturday.

According to recent reports, spaceX is now an ‘infrastructure’ manufacturer. For a long time, SpaceX has been synonymous with developing newer, larger, and ever-more-reusable rockets, Ars reports. But that began to change over the last decade with the introduction of Starlink, and the change has accelerated during the last 18 months as the company has pivoted to data and artificial intelligence. At last week’s UP.Summit conference in Florida, SpaceX’s vice president of launch, Kiko Dontchev, offered some of the most revealing comments to date about the company’s changing focus.

Sources indicate that from AI to Mars? … “In the last couple years, when I talk about SpaceX, yes, we are a rocket firm, but fundamentally we are an infrastructure company at this point,” Dontchev said. “We’re building infrastructure on the ground and low Earth orbit, soon on the Moon, and obviously eventually Mars.” However, Dontchev insisted that human settlement and Mars remain part of the core of SpaceX’s aspirations. “We have come to understand that this tool is critical to us accelerating our pace of innovation,” he said of artificial intelligence. “Without AI, I think we still would have gotten to the Moon. I think we still get to Mars with SI. We’re going to get there so much faster.”.

Available now, Pebblebee’s latest Android Find Hub tracker color drop might also be the first real miss, with the festive theme falling short of what it’s supposed to look like.

Pebblebee has been dropping limited-time color variants of its Clip 5 tracker for Android Find Hub and Apple Find My all year, with the latest release this week including “Cranberry” and “Champagne.”.

The newly introduced drop looks nice in marketing photos, but I will say, this is the first time I’ve felt the colors have missed the mark in person. “Cranberry” is a nice red color, but the bits of reflective sparkle shown in Pebblebee’s images don’t translate very well into real life. “Champagne” takes that a step further, with a very muted beige color that doesn’t have the shine seen in some of the listing photos.

They still look nice enough, just know you’re not getting the flashy, festive colors.

The good news, though, is that you’re still getting the same core hardware. USB-C rechargeable battery, support for Android Find Hub and Apple Find My, 130dB siren, and more, all for the usual $34.99.

The previous “Hotline Pink” and “Techno Lime” are still available for a limited time, and Pebblebee’s website has a Black Friday sale live, offering 20-30% off when you buy multiple trackers and use the code “BFCM26” at checkout.

‘It just looks like R2-D2’ — This latest gaming phone offers flagship specs and PC game emulation at a killer price, but its design is something else

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Products aimed at hardcore gamers aren’t exactly known for subtlety.
  • Industry observers note that the upcoming Redmagic 12 Pro is no exception.
  • Although they do offer dynamic RGB lighting, all the marketing material demonstrates them lit up in bright blue.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Products aimed at hardcore gamers aren’t exactly known for subtlety. Aggressive styling, bright RGB lighting, and bombastic colors are common whether you’re buying a gaming chair, a high-end controller, or even a dedicated gaming phone.

Industry observers note that the upcoming Redmagic 12 Pro is no exception. Its rectangular chassis is adorned with decorative elements and a smattering of colorful lights, designed to highlight its built-in liquid cooling. There’s a huge illuminated ring on the back panel, tracing the cooling loop that sits on top of the battery, along with a smaller rectangular shape and light bar next to the camera modules at the top, where the SoC is situated.

Although they do offer dynamic RGB lighting, all the marketing material demonstrates them lit up in bright blue. I’m sure it’s meant to make the phone look high-tech and futuristic, but honestly, it just looks like R2-D2 to me — especially that white model.

It’s a phone that makes a statement: “the person holding this is a gamer,” and while there’s definitely value in having a device that stands out from the crowd, I can already imagine the kind of looks that I would get pulling this big, flashy bar out of my pocket on the subway.

It’s a shame, as the rest of the package looks like strong value given the $949 / £799 starting price.

Industry observers note that the phone is powered by the latest and greatest Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 and up to 16GB of RAM, the same configuration found in the considerably more expensive Motorola Signature 27 and other cutting-edge flagships. The liquid cooling system, which works in tandem with a powerful fan and vapor chamber, should facilitate more reliable and sustained performance than other similarly specced devices.

It’s a great combination given the gaming focus: early hands-on reviews already suggest that this is the fastest-performing Android phone at the moment, allowing for steady frame rates in extremely intensive games like Wuthering Waves at high graphics settings.

Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android.

You’ll be able to appreciate all of it on the 185Hz refresh rate screen that, while not the biggest or brightest out there (at 6.85 inches and 5,000 nits peak), should deliver butter-smooth motion in supported games.

This is also one of the few new phones to launch with an under-screen selfie camera, so you don't even need to worry about a camera cutout or punch hole blocking your view and getting in the way of the action.

You’re also getting some physical advantages that aren’t present on other phones, namely physical trigger buttons that can be mapped to in-game inputs, cutting down on the need for an external mobile gamepad.

Industry observers note that then there’s the PC game emulation. The Redmagic 12 Pro comes with built-in software designed for running PC games from your Steam library. Not game streaming — these titles are running directly on the hardware.

And no, the performance isn’t going to be perfect, and battery life will take a serious hit, but testers have already got titles like Red Dead Redemption 2 running relatively smoothly, which feels seriously cutting-edge and is not something that I ever thought I would see on mobile phone hardware. I just wish all of this goodness was packed in a less… attention-grabbing shell.

The Redmagic 12 Pro hits shelves on November 18, with early-bird discount vouchers and free gifts available for those who pre-order now.

iOS 27.3 is coming next month, and during the beta so far there are three fresh features I’ve been using almost every day.

In a recent development, siri AI in iOS 27 brings major upgrades by providing world knowledge, personal context features, and being more conversational than ever. But one previously declared Siri improvement—an expanded set of actions for Apple apps—didn’t make the cut in iOS 27.0.

Now in iOS 27.3, though, Apple is rolling out its first set of new app actions for Siri AI.

Siri AI has newly introduced capabilities across apps like Calendar, Files, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather. It’s a massive step toward making voice-driven computing more powerful on Apple platforms, and I’ve had fun experimenting with everything new Siri can do.

Read more: iOS 27.3 expands Siri AI with many new capabilities across Apple apps.

Recent findings suggest that apple Health gets a massive overhaul in iOS 27.3, with a fresh design and new features that utilize Apple Intelligence for more personalized health insights. Per Apple:.

The updated experience includes a latest Insights tab that surfaces timely, holistic summaries spanning heart, sleep, readiness, fitness, vitals, and cycle tracking data throughout the day. A dedicated For You section delivers intelligent recommendations tailored to a user’s daily habits — such as practical guidance to adjust a wind-down routine following consecutive nights of interrupted sleep. The app pairs data with dynamic health content, offering educational videos and articles featuring Health app clinical experts.

In my testing so far, I’ve especially enjoyed getting up-to-date guidance every day on my health metrics, browsing the deep collection of new educational videos and articles, and understanding all the factors that contribute to longevity. I think Apple is moving the right direction with this update.

Read more: iOS 27.3 adds all-new Apple Health app, details here.

If you have an Apple Watch Series 12 or Apple Watch Ultra 4, iOS 27.3 adds a powerful fresh feature called Siri Recap that “ambiently takes notes on your conversations throughout your day and creates high-level Apple Intelligence–generated summaries that you can use later to jog your memory.”.

According to recent reports, "iOS 27.3 adds three fresh features I've used almost every day", "Apple Maps in iOS 27 has hidden new feature I’ve been loving". What's with these terrible clickbait titles lately? Did we go back to 2014?

Siri Recap functions like an outsourced short-term memory reserve. The data it collects is saved inside the Siri app in a new Recaps tab, where it lives for seven days and is then deleted—unless you manually save a specific recap.

In a recent development, so far in the beta, I’ve found the summaries Siri generates to strike a good balance of being helpful but not too invasive. It reminds me of key details, but there’s nothing I’ve seen that feels overly sensitive or personalized. That may change over time the more I use it, but so far I think this could prove a really valuable feature.

#166. Tech Report: It’s Time to Run an Audit of All the Cloud Storage Links You’ve Shared

📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (936 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 WIRED ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: It’s Time to Run an Audit of All the Cloud Storage Links You’ve Shared

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (936 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that cloud storage certainly has a lot going for it.
  • Then there's file sharing: Not too many years ago, swapping large amounts of data with other people meant dragging and dropping and running around with USB drives (and perhaps even mailing them).
  • Industry observers note that however, this comes with security risks attached.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that cloud storage certainly has a lot going for it. For a start, if you drop your laptop into the sink, it's likely that a lot of your crucial work will be backed up somewhere in the cloud, as long as you’re using services such as Google Drive, OneDrive, and iCloud.

Then there's file sharing: Not too many years ago, swapping large amounts of data with other people meant dragging and dropping and running around with USB drives (and perhaps even mailing them). Now, via a couple of clicks and a link, you can share just about anything with just about anyone, anywhere in the world.

Industry observers note that however, this comes with security risks attached. You don't want those links making their way to anyone they weren't intended for; otherwise, they’ve got access to your files and folders. They could potentially see what’s in them and maybe even make changes or delete files, depending on the permissions you’ve set.

It’s worth emphasizing that sharing files through these cloud storage services isn't inherently insecure—these shared links are actually very well protected by default. However, the longer they stick around, the bigger the risk gets. Your links could get mistakenly forwarded in an email, or one of your contacts could have their email account hacked.

Industry observers note that with that in mind, it’s prudent to run a regular audit on the cloud-sharing links you’ve got active. It shouldn’t take long: The apps involved usually make this pretty straightforward. Once you’ve closed a link down, no one else can get to it.

In a recent development, if you head to the Microsoft OneDrive portal on the web, you’ll see a Shared link in the navigation pane on the left: Click this, then select By you up at the top of the file list to see everything you’ve shared with other people. Use the Modified header if you want to sort the files and folders by the oldest or most recent.

Click the three dots next to any file or folder, then Manage access to control who can get to it. If you've shared the file with specific people, you can remove some or all of them; if the file or folder is shared more widely with just a link, clicking the trash can gets rid of it. You can also open up Office files to manage access there.

It’s worth knowing that when you opt to share a file in OneDrive on the web (via the three dots and Share), if you click the cog icon on the Share panel, you can set an expiration date for the sharing—which saves you the trouble of having to tidy it up afterward.

Sources indicate that if iCloud Drive is your cloud storage service of choice, once you’ve got the main interface up on the web, you can click Shared on the navigation pane on the left to go straight to the files and folders you’re sharing with other people. There’s no easy way to sort them, but you can use the search box up in the top right corner.

Click the three dots next to a file or folder, then Managed Shared File to make changes. The next screen lets you block access for specific contacts and change permissions (from editing to just viewing, for example). If you want to cancel the sharing altogether, click Stop sharing.

Unlike OneDrive, iCloud doesn’t give you any way of putting expiration periods on shared links, so you have to clear them up manually.

Recent findings suggest that dropbox is one of the more aggressive services when it comes to tidying up shared links, and if you use the Dropbox app you might see reminders to review the files and folders you’ve shared with others. From Dropbox on the web, click Shared in the left-hand navigation pane to see files and folders you’re right now sharing.

You can get quite a detailed breakdown here, including by Files or by Folders. Click the three dots next to any entry, then Share, to see the current sharing options: You can remove access for contacts one by one, or click the cog icon (top left) to find the Unshare button that ends all sharing completely.

Sources indicate that dropbox does have link expiration features built in: If you open the share settings whenever you’re sharing a file or folder, you’ll see Link expiry as one of the options. It’s an easy way to keep things tidy, provided the people you’re sharing the file or folder with get around to viewing it in time.

Google Drive isn't quite as on top of shared links as other cloud storage services. If you open up the web portal, there’s no easy-to-access list of everything you've shared. The closest thing to it is clicking the People filter and then choosing contacts to see files and folders you've shared with them specifically. If you pick Anyone with the link from the drop-down list, you’ll see everything shared with a simple link.

It has been revealed that to change the sharing settings for a file or folder, click on the three dots, then Share. Click the cog icon on the panel that pops up, then you can remove contacts as needed and turn the visible link off.

In a recent development, as with iCloud, there’s no link expiration feature you can rely on here, so shared files and folders can’t be set to become unshared after a certain time has elapsed. It’s a shame Google doesn’t make it as easy as it could be.

It has been revealed that this week, Perplexity has deployed its new proactive agentic AI feature called Teammates to the Mac. Perplexity Teammates were previously limited to iOS and the web.

Sources indicate that similar to Grok Bot, Perplexity Teammates are task-oriented proactive agentic AI threads that work for you without constantly being prompted. Meta Muse and ChatGPT Dots are similar, but use a single chat model rather than supporting multiple instances.

Here’s more about Perplexity Teammates:.

Sources indicate that teammates are a team of AI agents that own ongoing work. Give a teammate a responsibility, such as managing a growth campaign, triaging incoming bug reports, tracking your metrics, or researching a latest market, and it owns that work around the clock. It plans the tasks, brings in more agents when the work grows, and follows through until the result is ready for your review.

It has been revealed that access to Teammates right now requires a paid Perplexity Max subscription. The feature builds on top of Perplexity’s existing AI orchestration system.

#162. Analysis: Companies love a ‘rockstar’ CEO. Until they depend on one

📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (985 w)
📖 Baca
Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

Analysis: Companies love a ‘rockstar’ CEO. Until they depend on one

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (985 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When Jensen Huang quit, it struck me how swiftly the conversation shifted from his departure to whether Nvidia could manage without him.
  • Industry observers note that it wasn't about whether the organization had the technology, customers or talent to keep growing, but whether anyone else could do what Huang had been doing for the business.
  • Sources indicate that the manufacturer is hardly short of capable people.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Jensen Huang quit, it struck me how swiftly the conversation shifted from his departure to whether Nvidia could manage without him.

Industry observers note that it wasn't about whether the organization had the technology, customers or talent to keep growing, but whether anyone else could do what Huang had been doing for the business. That made me wonder: did investors believe in Nvidia, or just Huang?

Sources indicate that the manufacturer is hardly short of capable people. Interim CEO and Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has been with Nvidia since 2013. Nvidia has experienced engineers, established customer relationships and a leading position in the artificial intelligence chip market.

But, listening to guests on CNBC this week, I noticed how much of their concern was about the influence Huang had built outside Nvidia.

On Friday, just a day after Huang quit, Dylan Patel of SemiAnalysis told CNBC's "Squawk Box Asia" how Huang would persuade executives at smaller companies that make critical components to commit capacity to Nvidia. This helped it secure "the majority of supply chain capacity," he noted.

Without Huang, competitors could try to persuade those suppliers to allocate more capacity to them, Patel argued. And so the big question is, how much of Nvidia's advantage comes from its technology and how much comes from the relationships Huang built?

Recent findings suggest that there are obvious benefits to elevating CEOs to be rockstars. They can attract investors, open doors and give a firm a fresh identity. A charismatic leader attracts attention, reassures investors and makes a company's strategy easier to sell.

In a recent development, huang was particularly good at this. He helped shape the conversation about where AI was heading and made Nvidia central to it. Donning his trademark leather jacket, Huang took to stages around the world, courting world leaders to lay out his vision and explain why Nvidia would be at its center.

Before Huang resigned, Eric Ross told "Squawk Box Asia" that Huang "is the company.".

That may sound like an endorsement, but it also helps explain why his departure has raised so many questions.

Recent findings suggest that bernstein's Stacy Rasgon made an interesting distinction on the same program, also before Huang's departure. Nvidia had capable executives who could keep the business running, he noted. What was harder to replace was Huang's vision.

"They need a visionary like that," he said.

But for a organization whose valuation reflects not just what it sells but expectations of what AI could become, replacing that vision may prove harder than replacing the CEO.

Duncan Clark pointed to another part of Huang's job. He had become a bridge between Silicon Valley, Asia and Washington, and one of the most prominent voices for the wider AI industry.

Industry observers note that "I don't think you can replace him with one individual," Clark remarked on "Access Middle East" on Friday. Replacing him with multiple people is "going to take time, and it won't be the same," he added.

That distinction may be notable. Nvidia's board has begun a search for a permanent CEO and said it will consider both internal and external candidates. But whoever takes the job may not personally assume every role Huang had come to play around the tech giant. Some of his responsibilities and relationships could end up being spread across Nvidia's broader leadership team.

According to recent reports, for now, the board is emphasizing continuity. New chair Harvey Jones said Kress is backed by an experienced leadership team and that Nvidia expected its operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption. Kress, meanwhile, pointed to Nvidia's people and leadership team as strengths as the tech giant moves forward.

Other boards will be watching, particularly those that have allowed their CEOs to become the face of everything their companies do.

When a charismatic leader is the only person outsiders hear from, it becomes harder to convince them that anyone else can take over. There is also the question of accountability.

It has been revealed that clark described Nvidia's situation as a governance failure. And my colleague, "Squawk Box Europe" anchor Steve Sedgwick, raised a similar point on Friday about how corporate America has approached ESG.

Sources indicate that much of the political debate has focused on its environmental component, Steve stated. President Donald Trump has repeatedly attacked environmental and climate policies using phrases such as "green scam." But Steve questioned whether the governance element has been overlooked, particularly at some of America's biggest technology companies.

"When you have a 'Rockstar' CEO you need way more governance, NOT less," he mentioned, citing his recent conversations with CEOs and senior executives.

His point was that powerful leaders can come to believe the normal rules don't apply to them. Without strong governance to challenge them and prepare for their departure, the consequences for a organization can be far greater.

Linda Ford, chief executive of The Chartered Governance Institute in the U.K., said Nvidia highlighted what could happen "when a company's leadership is built around one person." She noted that Nvidia had never previously had a board chair, adding: "A high-profile leader can be an asset, but the board needs to work hard to protect its independence and provide the scrutiny shareholders are entitled to expect.".

Industry observers note that and that gets to the bigger problem. How easily can a board challenge a CEO who has delivered extraordinary success, particularly when investors have come to see that person as indispensable?

Industry observers note that companies spend years putting leaders in front of investors and customers and making them central to the business. But how much effort goes into making sure the company can function without them?

Industry observers note that nvidia now has to show that the business Huang built can stand on its own. Other boards might want to ask themselves whether they could say the same.

Scientists warn 1.5°C climate change threshold could arrive by 2029

💡 Key Takeaways
  • ANTALYA, Turkey—Amid upbeat green-tech pep talks and notices for happy hours at the annual United Nations COP31 climate change conference on Thursday, two new reports offered a stark reminder of how far the world remains from containing global warming.
  • Industry observers note that climate Action Tracker, a nonprofit group that analyzes climate policies, found that the planet is still on track to warm nearly 5° Fahrenheit by 2100, a rise that would devastate coral reefs, disrupt agriculture and forests and melt most of the world’s ice.
  • It has been revealed that when the Paris agreement was adopted, the average global temperature was projected to surpass the pact’s long-term threshold of 2.7° Fahrenheit above the preindustrial average around 2045.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

ANTALYA, Turkey—Amid upbeat green-tech pep talks and notices for happy hours at the annual United Nations COP31 climate change conference on Thursday, two new reports offered a stark reminder of how far the world remains from containing global warming.

Industry observers note that climate Action Tracker, a nonprofit group that analyzes climate policies, found that the planet is still on track to warm nearly 5° Fahrenheit by 2100, a rise that would devastate coral reefs, disrupt agriculture and forests and melt most of the world’s ice. In a separate bulletin, the European Union’s Copernicus climate change service reported that global warming has accelerated significantly since the 2015 Paris climate agreement.

It has been revealed that when the Paris agreement was adopted, the average global temperature was projected to surpass the pact’s long-term threshold of 2.7° Fahrenheit above the preindustrial average around 2045. After another decade of global climate summits, warming is now projected to cross that benchmark as soon as 2029, according to Copernicus.

According to recent reports, “This striking change suggests that global warming has accelerated in recent years,” the EU scientists wrote. Even without understanding every aspect of the recent rapid global temperature increase, “It is clear that the ever-growing concentrations of greenhouse gases emitted by human activity in the atmosphere remain the main driver of this trend.”.

The current level of warming has already triggered deadly and destructive floods, wildfires and catastrophic glacier collapses, said Swedish activist Greta Thunberg, who is attending the UN “Conferences of the Parties” climate talks, for the first time since 2021.

According to recent reports, “The climate crisis is a matter of life and death,” she remarked. “The actions from those in power here are completely detached from reality. As we speak, we are losing priceless lives, ecosystems and species that we will never get back.”.

Sarah Heck, a climate policy analyst with Climate Analytics, an international climate science and policy institute, stated governments have failed to meaningfully improve the outlook for end-of-century warming.

Industry observers note that “Our message is a stark one,” Heck stated. “Collective government action on climate change has stalled for the fifth consecutive year.” Efforts to speed up the shift away from fossil fuels have been negated by newly introduced oil and gas drilling projects and governments that are “delaying, weakening or rolling back their climate policies.”.

Even under the most optimistic scenario, assuming full implementation of existing policies and promises, global temperatures would rise 3.4° Fahrenheit above preindustrial levels by 2100, an increase climate scientists consider extremely dangerous.

While there has been progress on developing renewable energy sources, the “brutal truth is that these positive developments have not yet added up to bend the curve fast enough,” stated Niklas Höhne, a researcher with The New Climate Institute. Developing new oil and gas projects is a bit like discovering your food is burning and then turning up the stove instead of turning it off, he added.

Getting into the specifics of the current negotiations at COP31 surrounding global renewable goals, he noted that conference co-hosts Turkey and Australia have so far opposed including the word “clean” in connection with electrification targets.

“It’s very hard to understand, and the only explanation I can think of is their interest in fossil fuels,” Höhne said.

Australia is one of the world’s biggest coal exporters, and Turkey is a major coal consumer, with its power sector still highly dependent on the most climate-damaging fossil fuel. Even as they host this year’s climate conference, neither country has offered any specific plans to transition away from fossil fuels.

Bill Hare, the CEO of Climate Analytics, called out wealthy, developed countries for their lack of leadership on climate action, noting that European Union Commission President Ursula von der Leyen failed to mention anything about transitioning away from fossil fuels during her speech this week at COP31.

“Governments … at this COP have a stark choice,” Hare mentioned. If they continue supporting fossil fuels, “it would consign humanity and our ecosystems to insurmountable economic damage and irretrievable loss.”.

Bob Berwyn is an Austria-based reporter who has covered climate science and international climate policy for more than a decade. Previously, he reported on the environment, endangered species and public lands for several Colorado newspapers, and also worked as editor and assistant editor at community newspapers in the Colorado Rockies.

This story originally appeared on Inside Climate News.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Streaming giants are always finding latest ways to upgrade the user experience and adapt to evolving usage patterns, and Peacock is the latest platform to take its mobile app in a new direction with its biggest overhaul yet.

NBCUniversal announced a newly introduced era of the Peacock mobile app this week (November 11), showcasing a roster of fresh upgrades it hopes will not only enhance the experience, but increase user engagement and get viewers to spend more time browsing its seemingly endless library of titles.

The streamer says it's already started testing the newly introduced tools and will continue into 2027.

"Our ambition is for Peacock to be more than a place to watch," stated Jim Denney, Chief Product Officer, Global Streaming & NBCUniversal Media Group.

"With this upcoming mobile experience, we’re evolving Peacock into an entertainment platform that gives fans more ways to discover, participate, and strengthen their connection to their favorite stories, teams, and franchises, turning viewing into deeper engagement and lasting fandom and loyalty".

One of Peacock's most notable mobile upgrades is the addition of vertical video — which the platform says is integral to creating an experience that's separate from the one you get on a TV. Netflix jumped on this a while back, so it was only a matter of time before Peacock followed suit.

The latest Clips Feed exists as its own section, designed to give you a new means of discovering new titles across entertainment and sports that isn't just simply scrolling the homepage.

Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android.

Peacock is also launching its fresh Franchise Hubs as a way to browse more content but with a community or fandom focus. This section of the app packs interactive games, live moments, and relevant episodes and podcasts centered on specific franchises, from Minions, Love Island USA, The Traitors, and more.

As well as short-form video, Peacock is jumping on the AI bandwagon, introducing conversational AI search to give you another way to find newly introduced content. With this new function, you can browse titles by name or, if you can't decide what to watch but know what mood or theme you're looking for, it can pull up content based on that information, which you can refine as the conversation progresses.

Audience behavior evolves; there's no doubt, so in order for streaming platforms to adapt to these shifts, they have to make some changes.

It has been revealed that in the case of Spotify, for example, its Messages feature lifted a pain point with owners by allowing them to share music and podcasts with their friends directly in the Spotify app, rather than having to screenshot everything and send it to group chats on other platforms. Those kinds of features are genuinely helpful, but even then, Spotify has also plagued its in-app hubs with short-form video, and I want to see the back end of it.

When Netflix first unveiled its vertical video feeds, I wasn't surprised per se, but I certainly grimaced at the very thought of it. And now that more services are taking advantage of it, it's suddenly becoming the new norm.

But what gets under my skin most is how these vertical feeds are pitched to viewers. The streaming behemoths claim they're useful discovery tools, but at the crux of it, it's just another way to increase your screen time and how long you spend in apps. Doom-scrolling has taken over the social media landscape as it is; I don't need it to get in the way of how I browse movies and demonstrates.

Instead, I used price-tracking tools to identify products at or near record lows over the past five months.

Whether it’s nostalgia or a sense that technology has gotten a bit too pervasive, there’s no denying that Slate Auto appears to be tuned into the particular moment. The startup has a simple pitch: an affordable electric truck with just the basics, leaving owners to DIY and BYOD for everything else, all for a sub-$25,000 starting price.

Sources indicate that among the things Slate does without is an embedded infotainment system. The small digital display on the dashboard that highlights your speed and range is also where the backup camera appears if you engage reverse, and there are two USB-C ports that provide power but not connectivity, and that’s that. But there is a solution to getting lost, and it’s called “Screenless GPS.” Even though we don’t have a Slate truck to test it with, the OEM sent us a unit to review.

That’s right, it’s a good old spiral-bound road atlas! “We believe you should use the devices you know and love,” Slate says, and it reckons that maps worked just fine for past generations, so they should still work now.

According to recent reports, the Rand McNally 2027 Road Atlas isn’t quite as detailed as the maps being made for automotive navigation by companies like here. Those are designed to be read by computers, not people, with rich data on not just places of interest but also live traffic, road conditions, and the accuracy required for assisted and autonomous driving systems. Any OTA updates to the atlas must be applied by Post-it note, and its 154 pages cover the United States, Canada, and Mexico, in full color.

It has been revealed that the system is entirely portable, and it’s vehicle-agnostic: you can use it as easily in a Ford, Ferrari, or Fisker as in a Slate. Some might find the idea a little contrived, but having spent some time behind the wheel of the refreshingly simple truck, I think it fits the vibe perfectly. The automaker has added its screenless GPS system to its store for a limited time, and the review copy Slate sent Ars, along with the sticker pack, will be up for grabs in our end-of-year charity drive.
