📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, donald Trump Jr. agreed to end his advisory role with the prediction market Kalshi shortly after Trump Jr.’s venture capital firm made a large investment in its competitor, Polymarket.

In a recent development, “We have mutually agreed to end Don’s advisory role after his firm’s significant investment in a competitor this past summer. We are grateful for his contributions in helping us market Kalshi to more customers,” Kalshi said in a statement provided to Ars and other news outlets this week.

Trump Jr. may still have a financial interest in Kalshi, which has benefited from the Trump administration’s legal and regulatory support for prediction markets. Trump Jr. “was handed about $300,000 worth of equity in Kalshi after joining the prediction market platform as a strategic adviser in early 2025,” the Financial Times reported in June.

Sources indicate that “Kalshi’s donation of shares to the US president’s eldest son granted him a stake in the private company when it was valued at under $2 billion, less than a tenth of its $22 billion valuation in a funding round last month,” the Financial Times article stated. Kalshi is reportedly in talks for a latest funding round that would value it at $65 billion.

In a recent development, trump Jr. simultaneously has an interest in Polymarket via his role as a partner at 1789 Capital and as an advisor for Polymarket. The venture firm’s investment of $300 million in Polymarket was reported in August 2026, building on a smaller investment it made in Polymarket in August 2025.

“We have been discussing this internally since August when news of 1789’s investment in Polymarket became public,” a Kalshi spokesperson remarked. “Kalshi reached out to Don Jr. this fall to discuss his firm’s increased investment in our top competitor and his role on its advisory board… both parties understood that advising two competitors in a growing sector was complicating things for both of us.”.

The Trump administration has helped prediction markets grow with a permissive regulatory approach taken by the Commodity Futures Exchange Commission (CFTC). The CFTC has also sued 11 states in attempts to block state regulation of prediction markets, and filed briefs supporting Kalshi in its own cases against individual states. Attorneys general in many states accuse Kalshi of running an illegal gambling operation.

Kalshi co-founder and CEO Tarek Mansour told MS Now in an interview last month, “I get asked a lot about Don. I mean, I think that is a fair question… We are facing sort of an optics matter, I think.”.

Sources indicate that mansour claimed the relationship was not political, and it began as a way to market Kalshi at a time when it was much smaller and the public didn’t know much about prediction markets. “The key thing is we did it before the election. It is not a political decision, and it still isn’t. That’s the key thing,” Mansour remarked.

In fact, Kalshi named Trump Jr. as a strategic advisor over two months after the November 2024 presidential election. Mansour unveiled Trump Jr.’s appointment as strategic advisor in a post on January 13, 2025, a week before Donald Trump’s second inauguration.

Sources indicate that trump Jr. announced his position with Kalshi in an X post on the same day and indicated that he decided to help Kalshi on Election Day.

“On Election night at Mar-a-Lago, while biased outlets called the race a coin toss, my family and close friends used the prediction market Kalshi to know we won hours ahead of the fake news media,” Trump Jr. wrote at the time. “I immediately knew I had to contribute to their mission. Today, I am proud to announce that I am joining Kalshi as a strategic advisor.”.

After Mansour’s claim that “we did it before the election,” MS Now Host Stephanie Ruhle remarked, “But you didn’t say after, you know what, maybe this is a conflict of interest.”.

Industry observers note that mansour’s response suggested that Trump Jr. did not help Kalshi on regulatory matters. “We never had any policy regulatory involvement,” he mentioned. “It was always about getting the word out about prediction markets, how they work, looking at the forecasts, making sure people understand that it’s not a poll; it’s actually probabilities. That was always our focus… we have advisors from both sides of the aisle. We have Democratic advisors; we have Republican advisors.”.

Mansour noted Kalshi sought to work with anyone “that can help us get the message out… anyone who likes prediction markets, and Don does like prediction markets, we wanted to work with, because we wanted to get the word out about what prediction markets are. Don has 10 million followers on Twitter… he has a huge following, and he likes the idea of going direct, tweeting.”.

The Kalshi spokesperson stated this week that “Don Jr. has been a great marketing consultant for us—he helped us ‘go direct’ early on, which was a big part of our growth online.”.

It has been revealed that kalshi has also paid former US Senator Blanche Lincoln (D-Ark.) for lobbying services since 2024. As a Democratic senator in 2010, Lincoln helped write the law that now regulates prediction markets and mentioned the US should not let event contracts be used for sports gambling. As a Kalshi lobbyist, she supports event contracts based on the results of sporting contests and opposes state regulation of prediction markets.

Trump Media and Technology Group last year unveiled aims for a “Truth Predict” prediction market for Truth Social, but appears to have scaled back the initiative.

It has been revealed that US Senators Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) and Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.) raised concerns about Trump Jr.’s investments in Kalshi and Polymarket in a November 9 letter to White House Counsel Will Scharf. Warren and Merkley noted a recent incident of insider trading, in which a Trump teleprompter aide made over $100,000 betting on what Trump would say in prepared remarks on Kalshi’s mention markets, “should have been a wake-up call to the entire administration to enforce stronger ethics policies.”.

The CFTC settled charges against the teleprompter operator, Gabriel Perez, ordering him to disgorge profits of $107,539.02 and pay a civil monetary penalty of $65,000. Warren and Merkley said that despite the incident, “the White House continues to take no meaningful action to address these problems, all while the President and his family stand to personally profit from their participation in prediction markets.”.

The senators’ letter continued:.

For example, the President’s family has become even more entangled with the success of this industry. Earlier this year, Donald Trump Jr. became an advisor to Polymarket shortly before his venture capital firm made a $300 million investment in the organization. Trump Jr. likewise received an equity stake in Kalshi worth $300,000 in January 2025 and also joined the company as an advisor. Just last year, Trump Media confirmed it was developing its own prediction market called “Truth Predict” in partnership with Crypto.com.

The CFTC reportedly is close to bringing charges against Kalshi alleging that it didn’t properly notify the agency about dozens of new event contracts, but the CFTC is also continuing its fight against states trying to regulate prediction markets more strictly. The federal agency yesterday filed a lawsuit attempting to stop Arkansas from regulating Kalshi, after suing 10 other states in similar cases.

According to recent reports, kalshi has lost a number of cases in which US appeals courts and district courts refused to block state gambling laws. Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murrill yesterday touted a state court victory in which a judge issued a “temporary restraining order prohibiting Kalshi, Polymarket, Coinbase, Robinhood, and other ‘prediction market’ operators from continuing their unlicensed and unregulated illegal gambling in Louisiana.”.

Sources indicate that “It’s not complicated: if you aren’t a licensed gaming operator, you aren’t legal,” Murrill wrote. “Illegal gambling is a crime and is subject to jail time and significant penalties. Judges all over the country have overwhelmingly called this activity what it is: gambling. Kalshi’s and the other operators’ attempts to make up new words to evade state gambling laws, regulators, and taxes are not fooling anyone.”.

According to recent reports, kalshi argues that all its wagers—even ones that are functionally identical to sports bets—are event contracts, a type of swap that it says can only be regulated under federal law. Kalshi’s most significant win came against Upcoming Jersey in the US Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit, but the state is asking the Supreme Court to overturn the ruling. If the Supreme Court takes up the case, the Trump administration can be expected to weigh in on Kalshi’s behalf.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The outage lasted two weeks but full functionality is expected to resume soon.
  • It has been revealed that after two weeks in the dark, popular fan fiction website Archive of Our Own (AO3) is back online.
  • AO3 was taken offline at the end of October due to "evidence of a security incident" that OTW stated would result in two to four weeks of downtime.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The outage lasted two weeks but full functionality is expected to resume soon.

It has been revealed that after two weeks in the dark, popular fan fiction website Archive of Our Own (AO3) is back online. However, Organization for Transformative Works (OTW), the nonprofit organization that runs AO3, mentioned that some features have been temporarily disabled as a compromise to bring the site back earlier than the four-week mark, according to an upgrade post on the website. OTW said that features like icons and external work importing are currently disabled, while works can only be downloaded in HTML format. The organization clarified that these features will be restored and that no icons have been deleted.

AO3 was taken offline at the end of October due to "evidence of a security incident" that OTW stated would result in two to four weeks of downtime. Now that the open-source fan fiction repository is back online, its owners may still run into some challenges, according to OTW. The organization said it implemented an "intentional measure to help manage traffic," so users may experience delays with the website loading but can refresh to continue trying.

As for the site's data, OTW mentioned that none of it was deleted, adding that user "works, bookmarks, kudos, etc. are still safe." OTW also managed to pause AO3's draft deletion feature so that no drafts were deleted during the downtime. Users should log back in and check on their drafts, though, since the feature will turn back on starting November 29 so that drafts longer than 30 days old will be deleted.

According to recent reports, it's still unclear what the cause was, but OTW confirmed it was a "security incident" and that it would "not be sharing specifics about what mitigating changes are being made at this time." OTW added that it partnered with a security firm to review the incident and analyze the site to prevent future incidents. The update post noted that OTW has "no reason to believe that the user database was compromised, though we cannot rule out that possibility," recommending that users change passwords, update linked emails and change passwords of any other sites that share a password with AO3 accounts.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia has drawn a range of responses across Asia, with some governments moving to confirm chip supply commitments, while others are monitoring the impact on local projects or addressing ongoing investigations.
  • On Sunday, November 8, Nvidia’s board rolled out an independent investigation after reports that Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation; Huang admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip organization Megaspeed.
  • Nvidia’s influence extends far beyond the United States.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia has drawn a range of responses across Asia, with some governments moving to confirm chip supply commitments, while others are monitoring the impact on local projects or addressing ongoing investigations.

On Sunday, November 8, Nvidia’s board rolled out an independent investigation after reports that Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation; Huang admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip organization Megaspeed.

Nvidia’s influence extends far beyond the United States. The chip giant has built close ties with companies worldwide, particularly in Asia, where many of its key partners play crucial roles in the global AI industry.

Industry observers note that china’s foreign ministry rejected allegations on November 10 that a Chinese businesswoman linked to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was a spy, calling them groundless and a smear against Beijing. On Friday, a spokesperson reiterated opposition to export controls that disrupt global supply chains and stated the ministry was not aware of reports linking restricted Nvidia chips to a Shanghai data center associated with Alice Huang.

Huang’s exit has also raised uncertainty over more than $3 billion in Chinese AI computing projects reliant on Nvidia’s restricted processors, according to Reuters. Many of these chips are subject to U.S. export controls, making them difficult for Chinese companies to obtain.

In Singapore, authorities seized the passport of Alice Huang, former CEO of Singapore-based cloud computing organization Megaspeed, in June 2025 as part of an investigation into possible false declarations regarding server purchases, according to the Ministry of Home Affairs.

The Singapore ministry mentioned police took her passport to ensure she remained available for questioning, as she was not based in Singapore. The investigation examined whether servers shipped from Singapore to Malaysia were later sent to other countries without proper declaration.

It has been revealed that in February 2026, police found insufficient evidence to establish that Alice Huang had committed offenses related to the suspected false declarations, according to the ministry. However, authorities mentioned she had knowingly provided inaccurate information about her role at Megaspeed. She was issued a warning and barred from re-entering Singapore. Her passport was returned that month. Singapore also said it received limited assistance from U.S. authorities despite repeated requests for information about U.S. server maker Supermicro. Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs said its investigation into Megaspeed and six other individuals remains ongoing. The ministry did not identify the six individuals or specify their alleged roles in the case.

South Korea has close ties to Nvidia, with major chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix playing important roles in supplying memory chips used in its AI processors. Following Huang’s exit, South Korea’s Science Ministry stated Nvidia had reaffirmed its plan to supply 260,000 advanced GPUs to the country and to continue joint AI projects. Apart from that, South Korea’s government AI strategy council held an emergency meeting on Friday to assess the potential impact of Huang’s departure on the country’s AI industry, per a local media report.

Taiwan’s Economy Minister Kung Ming-shin said Huang’s departure was unlikely to significantly change the growth of the global AI industry, according to local media. Meanwhile, Taipei’s city government said Nvidia’s planned overseas headquarters in the city remained on track despite the leadership change. The manufacturer has met its contractual obligations so far, and officials said they would continue to support the project.

In Japan, the Industry Ministry said the government would closely monitor Nvidia following Huang’s resignation, describing the chipmaker as an notable player in Japan’s AI semiconductor industry, Reuters reported. Deputy chief cabinet secretary Masanao Ozaki said it was too early to assess the impact on the global AI industry, while stressing Japan’s commitment to ensuring a stable supply of semiconductors.

The bit began with Mulaney talking about hosting his children's friends, and how one child always seems to have an old man voice, not unlike Kennedy's.

Recent findings suggest that from there, Mulaney released into a full-on impression of Kennedy, rasping, "Stop the science! Robitussin, when taken during menstruation, will cause telekinesis.".

Mulaney then talked about how "no one likes [Kennedy] anymore," not even his right-wing friends who used to approve of Kennedy.

"You dumbass, your thing can't be the measles," Mulaney remarked. "That can't be your project, giving people the measles.".

Industry observers note that after riffing on Kennedy's poor health track record and his inability to live up to his father's legacy, Mulaney explained that he knew Kennedy during his early days in New York ("He wasn't hard to know"). He skewered everything from his work as an environmental lawyer to his organization Riverkeeper, which was in charge of keeping the Hudson River — "whose native fish is tied-off used condom" — clean.

Mulaney recalled how he and other comedians would perform at the annual Riverkeeper benefit, and how he once received a garbled voicemail from Kennedy thanking him for the performance.

In a recent development, while Mulaney described bombing at the benefit, this SNL monologue had the opposite effect. Watch the full set above. Here’s a HomeView feature that should come to every Apple device

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (499 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This week, Apple started shipping the HomeView, its first display made for the smart home.
  • On iOS, iPadOS, and macOS today – the only flexibility you have on dark mode is whether or not it automatically switches on towards night time.
  • Sources indicate that with HomeView, you can enable ambient dark mode.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This week, Apple started shipping the HomeView, its first display made for the smart home. On the HomeView, there’s one particularly nice feature that I’d love to see make its way to all Apple platforms: Ambient Dark Mode.

On iOS, iPadOS, and macOS today – the only flexibility you have on dark mode is whether or not it automatically switches on towards night time. While this is generally helpful and certainly appreciated, it isn’t super granular. Of course, you can adjust the time when it switches, but generally speaking its just a one time toggle.

Sources indicate that with HomeView, you can enable ambient dark mode. In display settings, once you enable automatic dark mode, there’s the usual two settings you’d see on other Apple platforms: sunrise to sunset, as well as a custom schedule. HomeView takes it a step further with ambient mode, where the ambient light sensor determines whether or not you should be in light or dark mode.

Of course, a sunrise to sunset schedule generally works for most cases. However, if you’re up late at night with your lights turned on, you still might prefer light mode in an instance where macOS would generally be in dark mode. Similarly, if you wake up later in the day with your curtains shut, at say 11am, you might not want to immediately see light mode on your phone the second you open your eyes.

Industry observers note that there are tons of good reasons for why someone would prefer ambient light-based automatic light and dark mode switching. HomeView software is the first Apple platform to enable this, and I’d love to see it come to iPhone, iPad, and Mac starting next year with OS 28.
